intro: Picture waking up, sliding open the balcony door, and finding the Si Racha sea in front of you, with the silhouette of Koh Loy floating in the bay, the soft sound of waves, and a coffee in a room that's roomier than you'd expect — Seaview Sriracha Hotel is a compact seafront hotel sitting on Jerm Jom Phon Road, on the seafront in central Si Racha, Chon Buri · What a lot of people talk about is the rooms — many have a private balcony overlooking the sea and Koh Loy, plus a sitting area, fridge, and microwave at prices that start at just a few thousand baht, which isn't easy to find for a sea-view room right in town · Open since around 2005 and renovated in 2020, it has a Thai-American restaurant, a cafe, a bar, a mini-mart, and free parking · You can walk to Koh Loy, Si Racha market, and the pier for boats to Koh Sichang, all nearby · Prices start at around THB 850/night on weekdays · Average score of about 8.6 from several hundred real reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com, and Traveloka

body.html: Who Seaview Sriracha is for, in a nutshell — if we had to sum it up in one line, Seaview Sriracha Hotel is a hotel for people who want to sleep right by the sea in the heart of Si Racha for a few thousand baht, without driving far out · It isn't a luxury resort with a rooftop pool or a full-service spa, and it isn't a big-brand hotel where everything is polished as if stamped from a template · Instead it's a compact seafront hotel that has been open since around 2005, renovated in 2020, and sits right on Jerm Jom Phon Road, so opening the balcony of many rooms puts the sea and the silhouette of Koh Loy right in front of you · Real reviews consistently point to the same fit: couples or families who want a seaside feel on a budget, travellers stopping over before catching a boat to Koh Sichang, and workers or anyone driving through Si Racha who wants a seafront bed for one night without paying a lot · Another group that says they were impressed is Bangkok folks looking for a quick weekend getaway nearby, since Si Racha is only about an hour and a half to two hours from Bangkok · You could say this is a hotel that plays on "by the sea at an accessible price," the trade-off being that you have to set your expectations on luxury and newness to match the price point

Location and getting around — this is Seaview Sriracha's main selling point, no question · The hotel is at 50-54 Jerm Jom Phon Road, on the seafront in the heart of Si Racha, and it's a few minutes' walk to Koh Loy and the bridge across to it, the town's landmark, with a shrine, viewpoints, and a popular spot to sit and watch the sunset · Within walking distance around the hotel are restaurants, coffee shops, markets, and several convenience stores, plus Charoen Pier and the pier for boats to Koh Sichang, which are very close · If you're planning a boat across to Koh Sichang for a day trip, this location is an advantage because you can walk straight from the hotel to the boat · Getting a bit further afield is still convenient: Robinson Si Racha and Central Sriracha are a short drive away, about 5–10 minutes · From Bangkok, driving via the motorway or Sukhumvit Road takes about an hour and a half to two hours depending on the time · U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is around 60 km away · One thing real reviews note is that the hotel's parking isn't right next to the building but about 200 metres away near the restaurant, so if you drive yourself, allow for a bit of a walk in and out, especially with a lot of luggage

"The room was way bigger than I expected, we got upgraded to the 5th floor and opened the balcony to a Koh Loy view right there, with two fridges, a microwave, a kettle, and a sofa — like getting a little studio for just over eight hundred baht for two. Great value for sleeping by the sea in the middle of town."

Room types and decor — Seaview Sriracha has about 60 rooms, split into several types by view and size · It starts with Superior Deluxe City View Balcony, a city-view room with a balcony and the cheapest option, good for people who don't mind missing the sea view · Moving up to Superior Room / Superior Deluxe Sea View Balcony, a sea-view room with a balcony overlooking Koh Loy, which is the type most people book and talk about most · And the largest is Superior Suite Sea View Balcony, a roomier suite that suits families or anyone who wants more usable space · What surprises a lot of people is that the rooms here are bigger than the price suggests and come with more than hotels in the same class — real reviews consistently mention that many rooms have a fridge (some even have two), a microwave, a kettle, a set of plates, bowls and spoons, a sofa, and a sitting area, more like getting a small apartment than a typical hotel room · The decor is simple and practical, not flashy in design · Every room has air conditioning, a TV, a private bathroom with a shower, and free Wi-Fi · Many reviews agree the rooms are clean and good value, though some note that certain furniture and items, like the bedspread, lamps, or TV remote, are starting to show their age along with the building · Anyone who cares about a sea view should ask for a Sea View room and a high floor at the time of booking, because the Koh Loy view from the upper floors is far more open than the lower ones

Facilities — let's be straight from the start: Seaview Sriracha is a compact hotel that has no swimming pool and no fitness or spa on site, so if you're after a resort-style stay with a pool to swim in, this place may not fit · But what it does have covers a short stay well · The highlight is a terrace and seafront area where you can sit, catch the breeze, and look out at Koh Loy, especially in the evening at sunset · There's an in-house mini-mart that's handy when you want a few snacks or small items without going out · There's a cafe and a bar for a drink · Other services include a 24-hour front desk, quick check-in and check-out, airport shuttle service, luggage storage, currency exchange, laundry service, a lift, free parking, and free Wi-Fi throughout · For a one- or two-night stay to see Si Racha or catch a boat to Koh Sichang, this is enough · But if you intend to stay several days living the resort life, you should consider somewhere with a pool and more activities instead

Food and dining — the hotel has an in-house restaurant serving both Thai and American food, with a seafront terrace zone where you can eat while looking out at Koh Loy · The seafront atmosphere in the evening is something many reviews like, because you get to eat with the sea breeze and the sunset · There's a cafe for coffee and drinks, and a bar to chill at in the evening · On breakfast, real reviews include both people who booked with breakfast and without — some chose to skip breakfast because there are plenty of restaurants and early coffee shops to walk to around the hotel · The upside of the central Si Racha location is that you'll never go hungry — just step out of the hotel and you'll find fresh seafood spots, rice-soup shops, coffee shops, and Si Racha market, which is known for local food · So a lot of people use the hotel as a base and head out to eat rather than dining in for every meal · Overall, food isn't the reason to come and eat in at Seaview Sriracha, but it's a supporting part that makes the stay more convenient, with the Si Racha town location doing a lot of the heavy lifting

Service — service is the most consistently praised aspect in real reviews · Many staff are mentioned as friendly, kind, lovely, and happy to help, from check-in to recommending restaurants and places to visit around town, all the way to helping with onward travel by boat to Koh Sichang · Some reviews mention getting upgraded to a higher floor without asking, which left them impressed beyond the price · The 24-hour front desk makes it easier for people arriving late or catching an early-morning boat · But to be straightforward, since this is a small hotel run simply, some services aren't as polished or systematic as a big-brand hotel, and when the hotel is full or there's a festival at Koh Loy, the speed can drop a bit · Overall, service is still a strength that brings people back for repeat stays

Real review voices (both praise and gripes) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com, Traveloka, and Pantip, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the sea and Koh Loy views from the balcony, which are lovely and hard to find at this price, rooms bigger than expected with plenty of amenities (fridge, microwave, sitting area), a central location within walking distance of Koh Loy and restaurants, friendly and kind staff, and value for money, which many rate as the biggest strength · On the gripes side: the most-mentioned thing is noise — both noise from neighbouring rooms that you sometimes hear, and music or activity from Koh Loy that carries up to the room on festival nights · Next is some furniture and items starting to show their age along with the building, such as a bed that creaks when you move, a faded bedspread and lamps, or a TV remote that doesn't work in some rooms; the parking being about 200 metres from the building; and minor cleanliness things like ants in the sugar that some reviews ran into · Most of these gripes are things you can fix by choosing the right room and setting your expectations to match the price point, rather than being big problems that keep people from coming back

"The staff were really lovely, the Koh Loy view from the balcony is genuinely beautiful, great value · The only downside was the night Koh Loy had an event and the music carried up to the room, plus the bed creaked a little when you moved. Next time I'll ask for a high floor on the quiet side instead."

Price comparison and value — starting prices for city-view and sea-view rooms are around THB 850/night on weekdays, climbing to about THB 1,200–1,600 on weekends or long holidays · A sea-view suite runs from around THB 1,500 up, depending on size and timing · Compared with other seafront stays in central Si Racha, like a loft-style boutique hotel that also starts at a few thousand baht, Seaview Sriracha feels very good value in terms of the room space and amenities you get, especially counting the fridge, microwave, and sitting area that make it feel like a small apartment · The trade-off is no pool and the age of the building · If you value "sleeping by the sea in the middle of town for a budget price, a spacious room, walking distance to Koh Loy" over luxury and full facilities, every baht you spend here pays off

Good to know before booking — a few things help make the stay go smoothly · One, if you really want the sea and Koh Loy view, ask for a Sea View Balcony room and a high floor at the time of booking, because the view from the upper floors is far more open than the lower ones · Two, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask whether Koh Loy has a festival during your stay, and request a room on the side that doesn't face the activity stage · Three, if you drive yourself, allow for the parking being about 200 metres from the building, and ask the staff about the most convenient spot to park · Four, check clearly whether the rate you book includes breakfast, because there are plenty of breakfast spots around the hotel — sometimes skipping breakfast and eating out can be better value · Five, during long holidays and the Kong Khao festival at Koh Loy (late April), Si Racha gets crowded and traffic is heavy, so book ahead and allow extra travel time · Six, choose free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet, since prices tend to change with the season

The verdict — from all the real review voices, Seaview Sriracha Hotel is the best fit for people who want to sleep by the sea in the heart of Si Racha on a few-thousand-baht budget, with a spacious room and walking distance to Koh Loy · The sea and Koh Loy view from the balcony, rooms that come with plenty of amenities like a small apartment, friendly staff, and a central location within walking distance of everything make it good value among budget seafront stays · If you're looking for a resort with a pool, a spa, and brand-new rooms that are flawless in every corner, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a resort in Pattaya or Bang Saen instead · But for a trip around Si Racha, catching a boat to Koh Sichang, or a seafront stopover near Bangkok without paying a lot — Seaview Sriracha is an option that meets that need well, at a price that's hard to match elsewhere, and that's why it keeps scoring high in reviews around here

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Seaview Sriracha Hotel

faq.q: Where is Seaview Sriracha Hotel, and what's within walking distance?
faq.a: The hotel is at 50-54 Jerm Jom Phon Road, on the seafront in the heart of Si Racha, Chon Buri · It's walking distance to Koh Loy, Si Racha market, and the pier for boats to Koh Sichang · It's near Wat Si Maha Racha, about 0.3 km, and around 5–10 minutes' drive from Robinson/Central Sriracha · From Bangkok it's about an hour and a half to two hours by car

faq.q: Does Seaview Sriracha Hotel have sea-view rooms, and what's the starting price?
faq.a: Yes, there are several sea-view rooms with a balcony overlooking Koh Loy, from Superior Sea View Balcony up to the Superior Suite · Prices start at around THB 850/night for a city-view room, and from about THB 1,050 up for a sea-view room on weekdays · Prices rise on weekends and long holidays, so book ahead and compare across platforms

faq.q: Does Seaview Sriracha Hotel have a swimming pool, and what facilities are there?
faq.a: The hotel has no swimming pool because it's a compact seafront hotel · But it has a Thai-American restaurant, a seafront terrace with a Koh Loy view, a cafe, a bar, an in-house mini-mart, a 24-hour front desk, airport shuttle service, currency exchange, a lift, free parking, and free Wi-Fi · Many rooms have a fridge, microwave, and a sitting area

faq.q: Who is Seaview Sriracha Hotel for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, families, and travellers who want to sleep by the sea in the heart of Si Racha on a few-thousand-baht budget, or anyone catching a boat to Koh Sichang · You get a spacious sea-view room within walking distance of Koh Loy and restaurants · If you're looking for a resort with a pool and full activities, a stay in Pattaya or Bang Saen may suit you better

faq.q: What about noise and parking at Seaview Sriracha?
faq.a: Many reviews mention that on some nights you hear noise from neighbouring rooms and festivals at Koh Loy, especially during events · If you're a light sleeper, we recommend asking for a high floor on the side that doesn't face the stage · As for parking, it's about 200 metres from the building, near the restaurant, so if you drive yourself, allow for the walk if you have a lot of luggage

faq.q: How do you get from Seaview Sriracha to Koh Sichang?
faq.a: The pier for boats to Koh Sichang is close to the hotel, within walking distance · You can walk from the hotel to catch a passenger boat across to Koh Sichang for an easy day trip · The hotel staff can help with boat schedules and travel · This location is great for anyone planning Koh Sichang as a highlight of their trip
